# Neptune stop notes

Lab notebook of the stop agent for `neptune`. Read `assets-src/shared/STOP-AGENT.md` first, then this.

## Log

- Start. Cloned, branch `agent/neptune`, merged `origin/main` at 9602aca. `npm ci` and `npm run build` pass. Rendered the stand-in `hold` and `terrain` comparisons at the draft tier and pushed them as the first looks.

## How the engine works (read once, kept here so it need not be read again)

- A stop = `src/stops/neptune/set.ts` (`createSet(ctx)` returns `StopSet { id, world, near?, sky?, update(state, shot, view), dispose }`) and `plan.ts` (`MoveParams`, `new StopPlan('neptune', fit, params)`). Mars is the pattern: `src/stops/mars/{set,plan,look,assets}.ts` with JSON beside them.
- Engine per sample: sky (with sky patches from `set.sky`, aim set by engine from `skyframe.json`), then `world` scene (set.world positioned at origin minus camera, rotated by `state.rotation`), then `near`, dust, cover. Post once on the average. Body pixels write alpha 1, sky 0 (G5 coverage). Diag views through `diagOut(...)` in `src/diagnostics/diag.ts`: texels (counted flag), layers, depth, flow.
- `state.view` is `orbit` or `terrain`. Terrain view: set.world origin = the spot on the globe, rotation = terrainFrame (x right, y normal, -z heading). Camera pose from `plan.terrain(t)`: position `(side*u, rise*u, -forward*u)` in camera heights around the fitted relief camera at origin, u from -0.5 to 0.5.
- Ending: `ending.retreat/lookback/fade` draw Neptune's set in the orbit view with `state.segment.stop !== plan.id`; Mars blends its light from `plan.lightDir` to `shot.sun.dir` (`lit`). LOOKBACK in `src/director/film.ts`: Neptune 31 deg off the Sun, distance 9 radii, vfov 34. So the crescent is seen at phase angle about 149 deg.
- Shared classes: `Planet` (`src/bodies/planet.ts`: wrap map, patch levels up to 6, storm turn about an axis by mask, light curve of 33 knots, ground haze, grazing haze), `HazeShell` (`src/bodies/haze.ts`), `MoonBody` (displaced, with baked lit map + mask), `Relief` (`src/terrain/relief.ts`: layers of color+alpha+dist with aprons, masks for mist/dust shift, valley fog march, air layer), `FarPoint`, `Cover` (engine-owned, set from plan colors).
- Approved pixels used as textures go through `inverseFilmic` and the lens vignette is undone on them (`uVignette`).
- Stand-in rings are a `RingGeometry` with 6 gaussian lines (shimmer risk). Neptune needs its own ring module.
- The loader counts texture bytes: w*h*4*(4/3 with mips), float data textures by byteLength. Limits: full 1400 MB, web 450 MB.
- Config: 30 fps. neptune.hold 151-156 s (frames 4530-4679, judged 4605), dive 156-159 (judged 4707), terrain 159-165 (judged 4860), rise 165-167.5 (judged 5006). Cover 0.5 s at 0.6 of dive, 0.4 of rise.

## Design decisions

- Orbit: own `NeptunePlanet` shader in `src/stops/neptune/` (copy of `src/bodies/planet.ts`, changed). Body Y axis = band axis `a` (globe quaternion in `src/stops/neptune/fit.json`). Spin about it; with omega = +a the visible surface moves right and down along the streaks. `hold.axis` near `a`, orbit opposite to the spin. Ring keeps its fitted normal.
- One RGBA texture per level: RGB = cloud-free deck albedo (hero divided by the light curve, tone coded), A = cirrus opacity. Cirrus colour is a computed white. Alpha from luminance `(hero - deck)/(white - deck)`. WebP with alpha saved with `exact=True`. Loader does not premultiply.
- Memory plan (full): wrap 8192x4096 RGBA = 179 MB, five 4096 patch levels at 89.5 MB = 447 MB, total 626 MB, leaving about 770 MB for relief layers, Triton, sky patches, ring.
- Cirrus is sampled where the view ray crosses a shell at radius about 1.004 (parallax in the dive). It streams by an extra latitude-dependent rotation about body Y with bounded fine turbulence, all zero at the judged frame (`elapsed = time - holdMid`).
- Soft shadow computed in the shader: 4 to 6 taps of cirrus alpha offset toward the Sun (`L_tangent * h / max(ndl, 0.15)`), modest strength. Deck = hero pixels where there is no cloud, generated cloud-free deck (image tool: remove cirrus and shadows from the hero, colour matched) under and beside clouds.
- Storm turns by rotating the deck lookup about the storm centre with falloff, zero at the judged frame.
- Haze: ground haze in the shader, a thin shell with the bright rim line at about 1.008 R, a wide halo, one layer across the disc edge on lit and night side. Night side never black. Crescent checked from the lookback angle (phase about 149 deg).
- Triton: real sphere, generated map, moves about 2 px per frame. Ring: own true 3D module with a smooth analytic, filtered profile so it does not shimmer. Hero sky patch for the hold. Sun as a small star with spikes via the plan light settings.
- Terrain: close image projected from its own camera onto a fitted sphere deck plus a raised cloud layer (mesh displaced by a height map). Motion as rigid rotations on the sphere reprojected into image coordinates (storm about its centre with falloff, cloud band about the band pole). Cloud shadows as a soft shadow map taken from the close image (approved over clean deck) travelling with the clouds. Clean deck via image tool. Aprons outpainted left, right and bottom on one extended canvas. Haze/air layer at the horizon. Terrain sky patch. Fit the horizon to get camera height over radius and set `dive.altitude` to match. Fine detail added in the dark lower-left foreground keeping approved pixels as the low frequencies.
- Dive and rise: patch levels 2x apart designed with a predictor. Blue haze cover streaming on both sides, thinning over 10 frames or more. Descent grade toward the terrain light. Rise ends with the whole body in frame, calm.

## Notes from the Builder (03:15 UTC, day 1)

- `public/assets/neptune/web/` at or under 35 MB on disk (not 40). Full stays 150 MB. The film is rendered from full.
- Engine requests as early as possible (they move the engine hash for every stop). Prefer stop-local code.
- The set is also on screen in the travel before the hold (body grows from a point of light: `FarPoint` as in the Mars set) and after the rise. Keep both free of pops. Judged in Phase 5.
- Ending (`ending.retreat`, `lookback`, `fade`): camera pulls away past Triton at close range, turns back, Neptune a thin blue crescent, Sun one bright star. The crescent needs a glowing limb and a night side that is not pure black. Triton's map must hold up larger than in the hero. Judged in Phase 5.

## Wrap pipeline (decided and measured, 03:15 UTC)

- Scripts: `assets-src/neptune/wrap/unproject.py` (2x hero to the band-aligned equirect window, `out/work/nep/wrap/hero-map.png` 4552x3641 with `hero-map-geo.npz`: mu, ndl, window), `curves.py` (deck and cloud light curves, `curves-measured.json`), `separate.py` (functions), `sepmap.py` (separation in map space, writes `hero-layers.npz`: deck albedo, alpha, weight).
- 2x hero: `tools/ml/upscale.py`, about 6 minutes, `checkmoved` PASS (PSNR 54.17 dB, SSIM 0.9989, flow p99 0.028 px).
- Deck albedo reference `A0 = (0.058, 0.215, 0.80)` scene-linear. scene = albedo * deckCurve(ndl), 33 knots over ndl -1..1. Night about (0.022, 0.034, 0.021), terminator 0.027/0.040/0.027, 0.27/0.33/0.25 at ndl 0.25, 0.71/0.81/0.79 at 0.5, 1.18/1.06/1.14 at 0.625, 1.58/1.14/1.32 at 1.
- Clouds are bluish in scene-linear: `K = (0.30, 0.39, 1.0)`. Cloud scene blue level by ndl knots `[-1,-0.2,0,0.06,0.125,0.19,0.25,0.31,0.375,0.44,0.5,0.56,0.69,1]` is `[0.02,0.02,0.05,0.15,0.35,0.77,1.26,1.7,2.0,2.3,2.5,2.7,3.0,3.2]`. The shader gets a second 33 knot curve for the cirrus.
- Separation: albedo = decode(map)/deckCurve; local floor (25th percentile) gives the deck hue; least squares unmix `C = p*hue + q*K`; zone m from `q/white`; deck = albedo outside the zone, anisotropic fill along longitude inside (normalized convolution at growing scales, clean pixels only, plus a grain tile); alpha from luminance. Recomposite error in the well lit part: mean 2.48 of 255, p99 37 (thin bright cloud cores). Telea inpainting was tried first and rejected (bright blobs, blur). First unmix with a white cloud colour left pale clouds in the deck, fixed with K.
- Hero-lit part of the sphere is only about lon -60..70, lat -47..35 (12 percent). Hero pixels fade out for mu < 0.42 and ndl < 0.2. Everything else is generated.
- Far side plan: separate layers. Deck tiles (cloud free, flat lit, band aligned) and cirrus tiles (white on black, alpha directly). Mid band: 3 tiles of 160 x 90 deg at lon 60, 180, 300. Poles: polar projection caps of radius 55 deg, north and south. All upscaled 2x. Detail of each tile kept as ratio to its low pass, colour set from a zonal target profile so tiles cannot differ in colour. Cross-fade overlaps (cirrus by max).
- Limb in the hero (sRGB): thin bright line at the disc edge, strongest at theta 45 to 90 deg (R to 240), into the twilight (theta 120 B 169, 135 B 55, 150 B 33), gone at 165 to 180. Outside glow at theta 45: B 235 at +3 px, 209 at +11, 166 at +25, 123 at +40, 85 at +70. Inside the sun side limb brightens over the last 20 to 30 px. Night side inside about (2, 6, 17). Plan: ground haze in the shader, thin bright core shell plus wide halo, forward scatter term (zero at the hold, strong in the lookback crescent).

## Orbit view work, 03:45 to 04:20 UTC

- Own atmosphere module `src/stops/neptune/air.ts`: three exponential layers plus one thin line shell, each with its own aimed light direction (`aim`, scaled by `home`) and `away` values `[from, to, gain]` that replace `dayFrom`, `dayTo` and the day gain when `home` is 0 (ending, far side). `home` is 1 near the hold view and 0 in the ending. Values in `src/stops/neptune/haze.json` (`air`, `limb`).
- `check/fit_air.py` (least squares on the outside limb profiles) was unstable. Values were set by hand from it. The dim inside limb was extinction by optically thick layers: depths bounded, `extinction` 0.5.
- Veil: the hero deck brightens toward the sunward limb (1.3 to 2 times at mu 0.45 to 0.25, about 3 times near the subsolar limb). The planet shader mixes toward `limb.veil` by `veilAmount * (1 - smoothstep(veilMu, mu)) * pow(smoothstep(veilSun.xy, dot(n, veilDir)), veilSun.z)`; `veilDir` is the Sun aimed by `veilAim` (toward theta 25 deg, because the hero's brightening is stronger at the right limb than at the top). `wrap/sepmap.py` divides the same veil out of the hero inset (reads `haze.json`), so after any veil change run `sepmap.py` then `assemble.py` (about 5 min).
- Limb terms added 04:10: `limb.shade` (air on the disc is switched off where the ground is unlit, except at mu < 0.1, times `home`; it removed a blue wash in the upper left twilight zone), `limb.twilight` (limb darkening for ndl 0 to 0.4, the hero is 0.5 times the curve there), `limb.dark` now applied after the air, direction theta -30 deg, wider with strength (the hero has a wide dark blue band inside a thin cyan line at the lower right limb, hero B 0.06 to 0.09 from rt 0.945 at theta -15 to -20), times `home`. `rim` raised to `[2.2, 4.4, 6]`, width 0.055 (hero rim line peaks 3 to 5 at rt 0.993 to 0.995). Hot spot layer `dayFrom` 0.9. `look.nightGain` 1.2 on the night knots of the deck curve (hero night 0.014 to 0.019 B, film was 0.012 to 0.016).
- The hero limb is not a circle: disc edge at rt 0.996 at theta 45 to 90 (inside the fitted sphere by 4 to 5 hero px), at rt 1.004 at theta 0, cyan line at rt 1.013 to 1.017 at theta -15 to -20, line at 1.005 to 1.007 at theta 135. Probably an oblate body (minor axis near theta 65 deg). The sphere is kept. Known weakness: limb offset up to 4 px at 1920x1080.
- Ring: fitted to hand-picked points of the hero's main strand (`out/work/nep/ringfit3.py`): `normal [0.1681, 0.9779, 0.1244]`, `centre [0.0533, 0.0532, -0.4902]` (rms 12.7 px; a centred ring gives 73 px). `centre` is scaled by `home`. Main strand radius 1.52. Hero strand points: far branch (95,1010) to (470,795), near branch (100,1050), (250,1195), (460,1260), (700,1365), (760,1385), right (2440,1160) to (2800,1395). Still open: the right branch is too faint and too regular in the film.
- Sky patch for the hold: `assets-src/neptune/sky/patch.py hold HERO FILL GLOW OUT`. Sky = hero minus a film frame rendered with the sky off (`sky.json` gain 0, review tier, copied to `out/work/nep/sky/glow-only.png`), hero's own sky from 1.07 radii out except where the film glow covers it, Triton's disc and the projected ring annulus; never excluded within 330 px of the Sun. Elsewhere a generated fill (`out/work/nep/sky/fill-t1.png`, take 1 of 6; recipe to be written in `sky/RECIPE.md`), low frequencies matched to the hero; outside the disc the fill's stars are replaced by the hero's own stars (top hat by line openings, so ring strands and the limb line are not copied), inside the disc the fill's stars are scaled to the hero's star energy. Margin 0.125: mirrored sky with the Sun removed (radial glow profile continued), blended over 110 px into a plain mirror at the border. Lossless WebP 3520x1980 (6.3 MB), web 1760x990 (1.9 MB). `sky.json` gain 1.538 = 1 / skyExposure. The engine draws the Sun core as a black dot in the patch.
- Triton: light aimed by `look.triton.aim` (times `home`). Film Triton measured 89 px radius against 95 in the hero, 8 px up and left (to check at the final tier).
- Check scripts: `check/profiles.py` (fine limb profiles), `check/outside.py` (compact table by theta), `check/ratio.py STILL OUT` (film over hero map in blue, red = film brighter, and a table of medians by ndl for mu > 0.45). At 04:05 the disc medians matched within 3 percent for ndl 0.1 to 0.8.
- Engine batch 1 merged (b4ae65c): sky patch `weight(time, view)` optional, faster sky pass. Software rasterizer computes both sides of an `if`; put costly conditional work in `for (int k = 0; k < (cond ? 1 : 0); k++)` with `textureGrad`.

## Terrain view (05:20 to 06:00 UTC)

Technique: the approved close image projected from its fitted camera onto a fitted sphere, split into deck, raised cloud layer and shadow factor. Class `Closeup` in `src/stops/neptune/closeup.ts`, numbers in `closeup.json`, fit in `close.json` (written by `terrain/horizon.py 30`).

- Fit: vfov 30 (the horizon does not constrain it; 30 keeps the hold's lens), pitch 20.627 down, roll -9.539, dip 12.409, radius 41.806 camera heights, nadir `[-0.155098, -0.922955, -0.352277]`, rms 0.029 degrees. Plan values: `horizonDeg 8.22, dipDeg 12.41, rollDeg 9.54`.
- Canvas (`terrain/cgeo.py`): the same camera with 1.75 times the tangent range, top edge shared with the approved frame. Approved box on a 4096x2304 canvas: x 878 to 3218, y 0 to 1317.
- Shader: one back side sphere of radius R(1 + glowTop) at the centre `nadir * (R + 1)`. Per pixel: ray against the deck sphere and the cloud slab (`cloudBase 0.07`, `cloudThickness 0.06` camera heights). Deck = core map inside the approved box, wide map outside, times the shadow factor read at the cloud advected point. Cloud found by a 10 step march through the slab against the height map with a secant step. Flow: clouds turn about the band axis (`streamPerSecond 0.035` heights per second, `streamShear 3`), the deck turns about the storm centre (`stormDegPerSecond 2`, falloff 1/(1+x^4), `stormRadius 1.1`). All zero at the judged time so frame 4860 is the approved image. Rays that miss the deck read the glow map, alpha 0. Expensive parts sit in `for` loops per the profiler finding, textures read with `textureGrad`.
- Maps: `terrain/layers.py` (see RECIPE). Canvas take 1 `gpt_image_2_6_flare` kept (centre aligned to 0.7 px), take 2 `seedream_5` rejected. Clean plate `clean-canvas-t1` kept, `clean-centre-t1` rejected. 2 of 6 takes used for each.
- Tone match of the apron: histogram match per channel inside the box, then log gain at the border carried outward at three blur sizes. Before that a plain gain clipped at 0.5 left a visible box seam (the generated canvas is far lighter than the approved image in the dark lower left).
- Sky: `sky/terrain.py` writes `close-glow.png` and `sky-terrain.webp`. The terrain set turns with the planet (`spinDegPerSecond 1.3`), so stars move about 4 degrees against the horizon each way during the view: the patch must be clean below the horizon. Mirrored about the horizon, no line left at the horizon.
- Plan: `terrain { vfov 30, forward 0.84, rise 0.31, side 0.05 }` is level flight of 0.9 camera heights along the view heading (level direction in camera axes `(0.0584, 0.3474, -0.9359)`). `dive.altitude 0.048` = 2 camera heights at the cover centre with `entryHeight 1.5` (g at the cover centre is 0.66).
- First results: judged frame equals the approved image in the compare at draft tier; sheet shows steady forward movement, the band comes toward the camera, the storm grows.

## Dive and rise (06:00 UTC on)

- Patch levels: six gnomonic levels round the dive spot (hero pixel 0.55, 0.52 = lon 0.23, lat -20.17), widths 96, 64, 40, 26, 16, 10 degrees at 4096 (web 2048), RGBA like the wrap (deck colour + cirrus opacity). `assets-src/neptune/patches/bake.py` writes them and `src/stops/neptune/patches.json`. Why six: with 96, 48, 24, 12 the dive passed G13 but rise frames 4988 to 4994 failed (3 to 9 percent soft), because the frame at altitude 0.4 reaches past the 24 degree level and the 48 degree level gives 0.9 texels per pixel there. Fade thresholds 1.1 to 1.6 texels per pixel of the parent.
- Detail: the wrap is 4 to 15 times too coarse for the last second before the cover. A 24 degree picture round the storm was generated from the wrap resample (prompt `prompts/patch-24.js`, take 1 `seedream_5` kept: same layout to 0.1 px median at 512 px, real cirrus filaments and spiral striations in the storm; take 2 `nano_banana_pro` returned the input unchanged). A second picture for the inner 12 degrees from the result (`prompts/patch-12.js`). `bake.py` matches each take to the wrap at low frequency (gain in linear light, blur 1/48 of the width), takes cloud opacity from the red channel against the wrap's deck, corrects its low frequencies to the wrap's opacity, divides the cloud out for the deck and uses the wrap's deck under thick cloud. Below the takes' own resolution it adds streak noise octaves (stretched 6 to 1 east to west) so that no level is a plain blow up.
- The level fetch in `planet.ts` is a zero or one pass `for` loop (profiler finding), six `if` blocks would all be computed.
- Cloud stream in the orbit view: the stream angle now follows time only within 2.6 s of the hold middle and eases to a stop 1.6 s later (`look.stream`). Reason: the cloud layer is sampled at the streamed direction, so with an unbounded stream the fine levels of the cloud layer sat 8 degrees (dive) to 20 degrees (rise) away from the camera at the cover.
- `rise.ahead 0.05` (was the dive's 0.14): the rise starts 2.9 degrees past the spot, so the frame after the cover stays inside the fine levels.
- Render time (06:25): with six levels a dive still near the cover took 120 to 200 s at the review tier (about 50 s before the patches). `layerAt` in `planet.ts` now computes every level weight first and fetches only the levels (and the wrap) whose final contribution is above zero, each inside a zero or one pass loop with `textureGrad`. Frame 4722: 65.8 s, pixel difference against the old shader mean 0.000, max 1 of 255.
- Cover (06:30): first values in `plan.ts`: `cover [0.3,0.5,0.98]`, `coverLow [0.05,0.13,0.42]`, `coverTerrain [0.42,0.62,1]`, `coverLowTerrain [0.035,0.08,0.26]`, `coverTop [0.3,0.06]`, `coverEdge [0.2,0.4]`, `coverEdgeRise [0.4,0.45]`, `coverShell [1.03,1.1]`, `coverRush` like Mars with lower contrast. ### R3's severe at 5006 (open item 125), the ring cut and dimmed at the globe's edge: what I know so far (no render yet)

- Geometry at 5006 (`end35/ring5006.ts`): camera 4.94 radii out, disc centre at (676, 485) px, radius 416 px, phase angle 89.6 degrees with the light from the top of the frame, so the lower half is the night side. Ring 1.28 to 1.92 radii, the camera 26.6 degrees over the ring plane, the light 53.2 degrees over it. The near arc of the ring passes IN FRONT of the lower half of the disc (ring at 3.5 to 3.9 radii from the camera, the globe's surface at 4.2 and more), so what crosses the dark disc is really in front, not showing through.
- The ring's own shader has no term that knows the silhouette. Its only planet term is the planet's shadow (`shadow`, distance from the sun axis under 0.985 to 1.025), and at this light the shadow does not reach the ring: the nearest ring point to the axis is 1.28 * sin(53.2) = 1.025. Draw order: planet opaque, ring additive (order 3, depth tested, no depth write), air shell additive (order 5, discarded inside impact 0.995). So in the buffer before the lens the ring's light should be the same on both sides of the silhouette.
- Measured in the final 5006 (`end35/ringstep.py`, `ringstep2.py`, medians B, G, R): sky beside the ring 11, 8, 4; ring off the disc 21 to 27, 15 to 20, 8 to 10; ring on the night disc 17 to 20, 9 to 11, 4 to 5; night disc without ring about 8 to 18, 3 to 7, 1 to 2. Across the silhouette at ring radius 1.45 to 1.75: inside (impact 0.93 to 0.98) 21 to 22, 12 to 13, 6; at 1.01 to 1.03: 32, 24, 13; at 1.08 to 1.10: 25, 18, 10. So the step is about 10 levels and the ring turns from blue to grey white, with a peak right at the limb (the air's line on the night side, about 6, 5, 3 over the ring further out).
- Suspected cause (to be proved with the `ungraded` view, with and without the ring): the lens chain develops with a filmic curve whose toe is convex (`filmic` in `src/post/chain.ts`, about 0.214 x + 17.9 x squared for small x). The same ring light added to the lifted sky (G 8) gives about twice the rise in the picture that it gives over the near black night side (G 3 to 5, R 1 to 2). So the ring reads dimmer and bluer on the disc, and the edge of that is the silhouette. Plus the limb line.

### Candidate for the 5006 severe: opacity for the ring (scratch tree `repo-end`, NOT committed, from 18:38)

- `ring.ts`: the ring's blend goes from additive to premultiplied (`CustomBlending`, colour ONE and ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA, alpha ZERO and ONE so the frame's alpha stays the body's own). The shader writes an opacity `solid = uSolid.x * (1 - exp(-density * uSolid.y))` with the density the largest channel of the ring's own strands times its edge, and adds `solid * uSolidGround` to the ring's light (a ring whose light grows with its opacity; the number is the level the lifted sky gives under the ring today, so the ring off the disc keeps its look). With `uSolid.x` 0 the output is the old one (opacity 0, nothing added), so the bytes should hold; to be proved by hash.
- `look.ts`: `ring.solid: { amount: 0.85, density: 125, ground: [0.0052, 0.0087, 0.0108] }` (first take). `set.ts`: one line after `ring.ending(...)`: `ring.solid(rising ? 1 : ending ? 1 - end : 0)`, so the weight is 1 in the rise, falls to 0 with the ending's own look over the first 30 frames of the retreat, and is 0 in the travel, the hold and the dive.
- Known and left: the air shell draws after the ring, so the thin line of the night limb still lies over the near arc.

A point X of it sits on the unit globe at Q (X - C) / R. So the twin height is 1 / R = 0.02392 radii (equal to 1 / cos(dip) - 1), and pitch and roll come with the nadir. ### MAIL 311 from the Builder (/root), 18:03 UTC, to every stop builder (word for word)

Decision d129, engine part E6 (handover_engineer builds it now).

What: in the dives and rises of a stop that opted in, the shutter of a frame is shortened so that the motion across it is at most 6 px at the point of the frame that moves most (config handover.maxBlurPx), eased back to the full shutter over the last 12 frames of a rise. Every other frame of the film keeps the full shutter.

Why: the critics of rounds 37 and 40 score the judged dive and rise frames as smear, severe (Earth 1857 "extreme radial zoom blur and low resolution stretching, blocky stepped streaks", Earth 2156 "dragged into parallel streaks and do not hold detail at native size", Mercury 1016 "smeared into long directional streaks"). The motion across the full shutter is 25 to 80 px there, because one steady move changes scale by 6 to 14 percent a frame. The path cannot be slower, so the shutter is shorter.

What it means for you:
1. Do not slow or bend your path to get less blur and do not build a blur cure of your own.
2. From the next round your judged dive and rise frames (Sun 247; Mercury 717, 1016; Venus 1287, 1586; Earth 1857, 2156; Mars 2427, 2726; Jupiter 2997, 3296; Saturn 3567, 3866; Uranus 4137, 4436; Neptune 4707, 5006) and every frame of the motion sheets are nearly as sharp as your draft frames. Every fault the blur hid will be seen: plate edges, a level that pops, thin texture, clouds as blobs, the place picture as a patch, a halo at the limb. Look at those two frames at the draft tier at native size (crops of about 700 px, not the whole frame resized) and put what you find on your list, worst first.
3. Nothing to merge yet. I tell you when E6 is on main.
No answer needed.

### 18:09 to 18:18 VM, the blue blobs of 4707 (item 10): cause proven, cure by code

- Far ground step committed and pushed as 98206197 (18:09), not named yet (the handover report with the haze is not run yet).
- Cause, measured. The draft frames of the dive and the rise counted for pixels with red 0 and blue over 120: 4682 7, 4686 126, 4690 1499, 4694 7171, 4698 12,911, 4702 13,225, 4706 9506, 4710 3638, 4714 440, 4718 126, 4722 and later 0; rise 4986 to 5016 up to 8. Pixels with red under 10, green under 40 and blue over 150 (pure blue): 4698 34, 4702 71, 4706 96. The mask at 4702 (`/tmp/b4702-mask.png`): the red 0 pixels are spread over the deep blue arms of the storm (not seen as a fault), the pure blue ones are the worms right of the eye (seen).
- "Depth" of a colour here: (grey minus smallest channel) over grey, grey = 0.3 r + 0.5 g + 0.2 b, on the frame taken back through the tone curve; 1 means a channel is at 0. Lit blue ground of the kept hold frame 4605: median 0.772, 90th percentile 0.839, 99th 0.879, 99.9th 0.894, none at 1. Frame 4680 the same (0.771, 0.838, 0.881, 0.897). With the plates in: 4690 99th 0.962, 99.9th 1.0, 0.32 percent at 1; 4698 99th 1.0, 1.45 percent at 1; 4707 99th 0.978, 0.62 percent at 1; 4714 99.9th 0.979; 4722 99.9th 0.893. So the plates come in deeper than the globe ever is, and a channel is cut at 0.
- Why: `planet.ts` shows a plate through the inverse of the near grade: divided by the grade's tint and gain, saturation times 1 over 0.45. The grade then comes in by its share (0 at height 2.06, 0.386 at 4707, 0.84 at 4721). The share of the grade that is not in yet shows the boosted colour as it is. Of the texels of the plates 16 to 42 percent would have a channel under 0 at full boost (26: 16.4 percent, 16: 41.9, 10: 42.4; computed from the files).
- Cure, by code: the depth the pixel will have on screen, depth times (1 over saturation at share 0, 1 at share 1), is passed through a soft limit (`patches.json` `place.vivid` [from, most]): under `from` nothing changes, above it the depth comes close to `most` and never passes it; the grey value of the pixel is kept. With the grade fully in only texels whose own depth is over `from` change.

### MAIL 340 from the Builder, 20:30 UTC, to every stop builder (word for word)

MAIL 340 from the Builder (/root), 20:30 UTC, to every stop builder. Three things, nothing to answer.

1. Main is a9ed9a0 (the tree of 42b1585c). New on it since 20:00 UTC: Saturn's surface view from code (32c488ab), Jupiter's surface view from code (9838e122), the test line that lets any stop set place.edgeIn in its own plan (bc2e4c41, asked by Mercury), the globe engineer's change of the own gain (42b1585c: the gain now multiplies the scene value; no stop on main sets it). Merge origin main into your branch before you name a commit; never rebase, never force.

2. The shutter of the dives and rises is set (decision d140 in kit/PROGRESS.md): handover.maxBlurPx 14 with handover.minShutter 0.5. While the fastest point of the frame moves less than 14 px across the open shutter the shutter is whole; above that it closes so the blur stays at 14 px, and never to less than half. So in the fastest frames of your dive and rise the blur is half of what you see today at the review and final tiers, and the draft tier does not change at all. handover_engineer to neptune_builder: plan E (the Builder's MAIL 369 e: E is the engine's one move and the default for all nine; a stop keeps a path of its own only for a need it shows me).
WHAT IT IS. In a dive and a rise the film's camera is the engine's, in both views: one glide over the whole segment between your two ends. Far end: hold(time - hold.start) going on (rise: after(time), the pose the travel leaves from). Near end: the first pose of your surface view, terrain(0), through your twin, carried back at its own velocity as a straight line (rise: the last pose carried on), reach at most handover.coastFrames (8) frames. One share for the log of the height, the direction about the place, the attitude and the field of view; its rate is one bell (flanks 0.4 and 0.4 of the segment, corners eased), zero at both seams. The close view is the same eye through the inverse of your twin. T (`at`) only says which view draws.
A STOP STILL SETS: hold(), terrain() (your overrides of those two stay, they are the ends), twin(), turn(), spin(); handover.dive.at, rise.at; path.sidestep, path.level, path.levelBy; path.rise and path.fall (the bell's flank shares of the whole segment; refused when the step of the rate would pass smooth.path.maxStep).

READ INSTEAD OF A CLOCK: plan.eyeHeight(time), the film's eye above the unit sphere in radii. That is the function I promised you as heightAt; the name changed because Mercury holds a private heightAt.
HOW IT LANDS: my block of the config gets `handover.ownPath`, the list of stops still on their own path; in my first commit (due 00:45 UTC) every stop but Mars, so your bytes do not change when it goes onto main. `--diag onemove` draws any stop on E without touching the list. You go onto E by deleting "neptune" from that list in a commit of your own (that one edit in my block is yours) and dropping the overrides.
NEPTUNE. The `at` that keeps your present height at T (0.0269 and 0.0281 radii): dive 0.850 (T in 4756, now 4758), rise 0.136 (T in 4960, now 4956). The harness reads your worst step now as 0.106 and 0.172 of the mean (limit 0.08). placeFrames 0 and skyFrames 0 stay valid, with a test. ## NOTE 501 from the Builder (/root), arrived 03:36 VM, high priority, word for word

NOTE 501 to every stop builder and globe_engineer, from the Builder, 03:38 UTC. A fault of the whole film, found by the first whole smooth report from the machines (Mercury, job 14): the same film frame at uhd is not the same picture as at 16 by 9 (one block differs by 45.8 levels at 713, limit 12).
CAUSE, found by mercury_builder: every globe brings its plate levels and its fine levels in by the texels of the parent a pixel of the format (uPatchFade 1.1 to 1.7 against gd * scale * size, gd from dFdx and dFdy). At uhd a pixel is half as large, so every level comes in at twice the height; at preview at half the height; in the live player it depends on the window. Brandon captures at uhd, so he gets another film than the one we judge. The term is in src/bodies/planet.ts (globe_engineer) and in the own globe code of mercury, venus, earth, jupiter, uranus, neptune and the Sun (src/stops/<stop>/globe.ts or planet.ts).
RULING (plan F: whatever blends does so by distance, height or angle): the measure is texels of the parent a 1080th of the frame height, an angle, not a pixel. In practice one factor, the height of the drawing buffer in pixels over 1080 (1 at 16 by 9, 2 at uhd, 0.5 at preview), multiplied into the density that a fade reads (parent, texels, fine, thin, cap, whatever your code calls it) and into nothing that only picks a mip for sampling.
PROOF, both by you before you name the commit: (a) at 16 by 9 the factor is 1 and every byte stays: the hashes of your own draft frames before and after are equal. (b) at uhd the picture becomes the 16 by 9 picture, only finer: npm run smooth -- --stop ID --only parity on your tree (seven frames), limits mean 12, coarse mean 3.2, one block 12, frame level 2.2.
THE SAME RULE holds for every other number in your stop that is counted in pixels and can be seen: the width of a feather, the radius of a glow, a threshold of a size on screen, a point size. If your parity is still red with the factor in, the panel names the block: find the term.
WHO: each stop builder, in the commit you name next (mercury_builder has it in work). globe_engineer: src/bodies/planet.ts and anything else under src/bodies and src/core that reads a density a pixel, as one commit on newest main (6884e80 or later), then ask me for the engine proof and say which stops draw with the shared code. saturn_coder and mars_place_builder: check your place code for the same kind of term and say what you found.
A red parity is a severe item in a stop's round.

## NOTE 504 from the Builder (/root), arrived 03:48 VM, high priority, word for word

NOTE 504 to every stop builder, from the Builder, 03:51 UTC. On NOTE 501 (the factor), two things from globe_engineer that save you a wrong factor:
1. Do NOT take the factor from view.format in the pass that draws a place picture. There view.format is the layout's, larger by the picture's scale (2 at 16 by 9), so view.format.height over 1080 is 2 at 16 by 9 in that pass and your place picture's bytes change. And the edge limit (handover.place.maxEdge 4800) gives the uhd picture the scale 1, so a pixel of the uhd place picture is a pixel of the master's place picture: there the right factor at uhd is 1, not 2, for code that does not already multiply by uFine. Code that multiplies its density by uFine (the terrain shaders) needs the format's factor alone.
2. The shared helper, in proof now and on main as soon as it is clean (agent/engine-globe, globe_engineer names the commit): src/core/frame.ts with frameUniform (the format's height over the master's, set by the engine in applySize, usable as a uniform), setPass (the engine sets it while a place picture is drawn) and bufferFrame() (the two multiplied, for code that reads a density a pixel of the buffer and knows nothing of uFine).
RULING: use the helper, not a factor of your own. If your cure is already written with your own uniform (uranus_builder: seen.ts), keep working with it and swap its source to the helper when I tell you it is on main; that swap changes no byte and needs no new proof beyond the hashes. If you have not started, fetch globe_engineer's commit when it names it and write against the helper. Stops with no place picture left (plan F) have only case 1's last sentence to mind.

## MAIL 508 from the Builder (/root), read 04:00 VM (it came while I waited on the render, between 03:56 and 04:00), high priority, word for word

MAIL 508 from the Builder (/root), to every stop builder. A timetable, so the rounds with critics can start. Clock: 03:58 UTC now (read yours with date -u; some VMs run minutes ahead).

Why: 22 hours after Brandon's first note no stop has a named commit with a green smooth report, so no critic has seen the new work. The kit's rule: no single item may hold up the film, and each stop has three rounds for this note. The second note's rule: a stop's round starts on a named commit with a clean take check and a green smooth report; a stop whose third named commit is still red goes into its round with the red measures as severe issues.

1. Your FIRST NAMED COMMIT is due by 07:00 UTC (the Sun: 08:00 UTC, because its ground is new from nothing). One commit on your branch, on top of the newest origin/main you can merge (7a6f888 or later). Its mail starts with the word NAMED and the full sha.
2. If no NAMED mail is here at the hour, the newest head of your branch that builds and passes its tests is taken as your first named commit as it stands. So push whole states, not halves.
3. What NAMED means: this is the build you would show a critic today. At the least: (a) dive and rise are each one move (plan E), by the engine's pace or by your own path with your own lines of npm run smooth -- --stop ID --only path; (b) nothing comes in by the clock, the place picture is off in both moves (plan F); (c) NOTE 501: nothing comes in by the pixel (the shared helper src/core/frame.ts goes onto main as soon as its proof is back, about 05:15 UTC; if you need the factor earlier, use the frame height over 1080 in your own files and move to the helper after); (d) the judged hold and surface view at the final tier beside the kept stills: equal bytes, or the pair as a picture with one line saying what changed and why; (e) the net size of your three folders against main.
4. The NAMED mail also carries, in this order and short: your own smooth lines (path, pictures, parity: green or the red lines as they print), the frames that change outside your dive and rise, and your own list of what is still wrong, worst first. Reds do not hold the mail back. A red that you know and name costs nothing; one you hide costs a round.
5. After NAMED: I cut the proof tree, my machines run the take check and the whole report (about 45 minutes). Green: the take goes onto main and your round starts at once with fresh critics. Red: you get the report and name your second commit within 90 minutes of it; the third goes into its round as it is.
6. While your commit is on the machines you go on with your own list. Work for after the first round is not lost: a round ends with fixes.
7. Everything already ruled stands (the orders in my earlier mails to you, the size rule, one owner per folder, looks pushed at least every 30 minutes). Where an earlier mail said ONE commit or ONE head, that commit or head is your named commit.

No answer is needed to this mail. Send NAMED when you have it.

## MAIL 526 from the Builder (/root), arrived 04:52 VM, high priority, word for word

MAIL 526 from the Builder (/root), 04:52 UTC, one mail to every stop builder and to handover_engineer: THE SEAM WITH THE SURFACE VIEW. A ruling (d196).

FOUND on Mars's rise at 60 pictures a second. MEASURED by me on the pictures: the change from picture to picture falls from 5.3 to 2.7 within three capture frames after the seam (film frame 2670) and is at 8.8 four later. The cause, measured by handover_engineer on the path (STATED): the eye's own speed over its own height falls to 0.33 of the surface view's at 2671 + 1/2 and is at 2.2 five capture frames later. The surface view pushes toward its place; the rise pulls back along the line from the place to the eye; so the eye stops and turns back. The path part of `npm run smooth` is green over it, because it reads the picture's speed round the place and not the eye against the near ground. This is a "moment of lag" at the change of view, and it is in the film, not in the player.

THE RULE. Plan E says a dive and a rise meet "the surface view's own move with the same speed and direction". That holds for the frames after the seam as well as at it: across each seam with the surface view the eye's speed over its own height never dips and never turns back. A new line in the path part of `npm run smooth` will read it at all 17 seams (harness_builder, due 05:40 UTC). Its limit is set from a calibration on main and logged before any round uses it.

WHERE IT IS CURED: in the surface view's own path, which is yours. Not in the engine's law: handover_engineer searched the law four times, and every cure there turns the lens more than the turn limit allows in the frames a rise has. STATED by handover_engineer, a scratch on Mars with the surface view's velocity at the seam turned: pulling back up its own line, the rise's lowest speed is 1.05 and it never turns back; across its lens 0.95 and 1.02; 45 degrees off 0.53; pushing at its place 0.33. A dive arrives down the surface view's way (0.98 and more on the one move).

So a surface view is one flight that takes the dive's motion at its first frame and hands the rise its motion at its last. Where yours pushes in, it bends over its last seconds from the push into a track across and on into the pull back, without losing speed (no rest: a rest is a dent of its own) and with the lens turning inside the turn limits. Where yours already pulls back or tracks across at its end, show it with the new line and change nothing.

WHAT MUST NOT CHANGE: the picture of the judged surface frame. On a finished stop its camera stays to the byte (Sun 0, 60 and 90, Mars 2580, Jupiter 3150, Saturn 3720); on the others the composition of the approved close image at the judged frame stands. The bend lives after the judged frame. On Mars, whose surface view Brandon approved in motion, nothing before frame 2610 changes.

## MAIL 596 from the Builder (/root), 09:04 UTC, high priority, to the nine stop builders, word for word

MAIL 596 from the Builder (/root) to the nine stop builders. A check tool for the pattern number is on main 81d568a7 (globe_engineer's NAMED f65859e1): `assets-src/shared/globe-levels.py`. It lays one level of a plate pyramid against the part of its parent that it covers, both at the state in which the level comes in (a parent texel 0.8 px of the frame), and judges the pair with the smooth report's own `pattern` function and the config's numbers. Seconds, no render. Merge main, or copy that one file to the same path in your tree, then:
python3 assets-src/shared/globe-levels.py --dir public/assets/ID/full --json src/stops/ID/FILE.json [--key levels] [--suffix=-dive] [--pairs 0-1,1-3] [--panel out.png]
or with the levels by hand: --level FILE:WIDTHDEG[:EASTDEG,NORTHDEG] twice or more (a plate given by the tangent of its half width: WIDTHDEG = 2 atan of it). One line a pair, OVER and exit 1 above smooth.pictures.maxPattern. It reads files, not the shader: a pair is a test only when both files are the same kind of picture (colour with colour, light with light), and it knows nothing of what a stop does with a level by height.

MEASURED by me on main's Mars (the old plates): 0.06, 0.00, 0.06, 0.00, 0.00, 0.00, 0.00 in 3.5 s, as its author states. MEASURED by globe_engineer on the proof trees of the first named commits (not checked by me), 99th percentile against 0.45:
- Mars b83618ec: patch-19 to land-8p5 1.19 OVER, land-3p8 to land-1p6 0.69 OVER, land-1p6 to land-0p7 0.59 OVER, land-0p7 to land-0p3 0.98 OVER; the other three pairs 0.00 to 0.09. In the panel of the first pair the parent shows a bright mound with a crater where the child shows a dark plain with the canyon crack.
- Mercury 9b5f55cd: patch-1 to patch-2 1.09 OVER (dive), patch-2 to patch-3r 0.70 OVER (rise), the others 0.01 to 0.02.
- Uranus 9a369939: every pair 0.00 to 0.01. Its red is not in the plates.
- Venus 3b52b0eb: colour 0.01 and 0.02; light a to b 0.20 and 0.13; light b to d 1.12 and 1.10 OVER, with a caution (the two light plates may not be the same quantity).
- Not run: Saturn, Jupiter, Earth, Neptune, the Sun.

RULED. Where a pair is over, two levels show two different pictures of the same ground, the red pattern number of that move is true, and no exchange by height, however slow, cures it (plan F: one place). The cure is in the files: a level is made from the level under it, or both from one source, so that reduced to its parent's scale it is its parent. Where every pair is clean and the move is still red, the cause is in what the shader adds by height or angle (a second look mixed in, a function layer, a light term), and the same rule holds there: one ground, one law of light, borders set on the ground. No limit moves.

Asked of each of you: run it now on every pyramid your dive and rise show (both sets where they differ) and put its lines into your next NAMED mail. A pair over the limit is named there as red, with its cure. This changes no due time.

   has an end where the last of the leaving picture goes out in one step (f without bound).

1. MEASURED with the handover report as the engineer did (npm run -s handover -- --stop neptune --kind rise --tier draft
   --only frames --format preview; 75 frames, 704 s; preview drafts, where the engineer read drafts at 1920 by 1080), on

   IN PLACE: level 3.61 into 5001, colour 6.57 into 5002: would pass, with 1.43 of room in the colour.
   So the present state reads as main 2bc36ce6 did for the engineer (3.83 and 6.64 into 5001), though the picture under it
   is another: there the place went out in ten frames, here it is the grade of the fall alone.
   The step in place of the blue by frame (rise, heights in radii):
     4985 (0.256) 0.34, 4988 (0.343) 1.51, 4990 2.57, 4992 (0.507) 3.35, 4994 3.86, 4996 (0.749) 4.49, 4998 5.46, 5000 (1.108)
     6.21, 5001 6.47, 5002 (1.348) 6.57, 5003 6.23, 5004 4.98, 5005 3.18, 5006 (1.948) 1.28, 5007 0.73.
   Under 0.25 radii and over 1.95 the step is 0.4 to 1.0. So what stands over that is the grade, and it is not even: most of
   it falls between 0.9 and 1.6 radii.
2. THE CAUSE. The share of the grade ran as a smoothstep of the logarithm of the height between 1.9 and 0.25 radii, and
   the share scales the POWER a tone under the pivot is raised to (1 at the top, 2.6, 3.1, 3.7 at the bottom). The first of
   a power takes most of a tone's level. From the two reports (out/work/nep/weave/response.py: the step in place less its
   floor, summed from the top down, against the share at each frame): the first 0.1 of the share takes 0.21 to 0.24 of all
   the grade takes, the first 0.3 takes 0.48 to 0.53, the upper half of the share only 0.29 to 0.36. The rate falls from
   about 2.2 at share 0 to 0.75 at share 0.45 and stays there.
3. FIRST FORM OF A CURE (trial e1): the share run so that a tone which the whole grade takes to 0.2 of its level falls
   evenly with the logarithm of the height, set in and out over 0.15 of the range. 4605 and 4860 keep their bytes (the
   share is 0 and 1 exactly outside the range). Rise by the report: on the body level 3.08 into 4970, colour 3.5 into 4972;
   in place level 3.11 into 4989, colour 6.19 into 4989. The top is down (5002: 5.47 for 6.57) and a new peak stands at
   the bottom (4988, 4989: 6.2), with 4.0 between. A single tone is not the picture: the rate does not go on falling with
   the share, it stays at 0.75.
4. SECOND FORM (trial e2, rendering 18:27): the share as way times (0.42 + 0.58 times way), way being the share of the
   logarithm of the height, set in and out over 0.15 of itself at either end. Against the measured rate this is even to
   about 2 parts in 100 (way 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 give 0.27, 0.52, 0.75 of the grade's whole).

A. WHAT THE WEB SET AND THE DRAFT TIER TAKE (measured)

A1. A FAULT OF MINE, found 22:13. It is the black globe you rendered, and I take it to be Brandon's "really bad": the web set's dive patch levels have a black deck. In all six web files patch-96 to patch-10 the deck colour is 0.1, 0.3, 4.6 of 255 wherever the cirrus opacity is 0 (59 to 83 percent of each level); the full set holds 49, 92, 173 there. Cause: `assets-src/neptune/patches/bake.py` halved the RGBA picture with the image library's resize, which weights colour by opacity; the deck lives in RGB where the opacity is 0, so it came back black. The levels cover the globe to 48 degrees round the place, most of the lit face at the hold. Three of the six are drawn today (96, 64, 40); their blobs are the same in b0b87889, on main and on my head. No proof of mine ever rendered the web set; that is the miss.
Cured in my working tree (not committed yet): the six web files rewritten from the full ones channel by channel (`patches/web.py`), `bake.py` corrected. Proof, draft, 1920 by 1080, mean difference to the full set of 255: 4605 16.38 before, 1.24 after; 4707 35.37, 1.28; 4988 8.25, 1.01. Pictures wf3-4605, wf3-4605-storm, wf3-4707 (web as on main | web cured | full set). Net of my folders goes down 1.8 MB.
A2. Every other web map I compared texel for texel with the full one halved: wrap, hold, wrap-mend, far, flow, rings, Triton agree to the codec (under 3.5 of 255 on the mean). Smaller in the web set (web | full): wrap 4096x2048 | 8192x4096; the patch levels 2048 | 4096 square; hold 2276x1821 | 4552x3641; flow 2048x1024 | 4096x2048; far 1024x512 | 2048x1024; wrap-mend 512 | 1024; sky-hold 2464x1386 | 4928x2772; sky-terrain 1760x990 | 3520x1980; Triton 2048x1024 | 4096x2048; ring-bands 2048x256 | 4096x512. The scene from code is the same in both sets.
A3. Still open after the cure: the globe's levels are chosen by texels per pixel (planet.ts line 121), so with half the texels each finer level comes in at about twice the height. At 4605 the web set already shows the levels' spiral grooves inside the eye where the full set shows the hold map (difference in the eye's box 7.3 of 255 against 1.24 for the frame; picture wf3-4605-storm, middle against right). So "4605 to the byte" was only ever true of the full set. This goes away with the plan below (one field, no levels with a picture of their own).
A4. The draft tier: my stop reads no tier and no sample number. Nothing of mine is a noise or a dither that averages out, and the haze of the limb and the air are closed forms. What the draft takes is what the engine makes from samples: all edge smoothing (the engine has no other; thin hard things step and crawl: limb line, horizon, cirrus streaks, cumulus puffs, rings, stars) and the whole shutter blur. 4980 to 4995 are blurred over 38 to 44 px of 960 in the film and are sharp in the player, so every exchange is seen there frame by frame. Rule I take from it: nothing may be cured by a jitter over samples, because the player draws once.

B. THE CAUSE OF (c), WHICH IS THE CRITICS' (2) AND (3)

Two different cloud fields stand at the place. M is the globe's map, painted from the hero. S is the surface scene from code, whose eye, pale plain and cumulus ridge were laid to the approved close image. Control (the map alone, 4980 to 4995, sheet c-mapA-storm against the present state c-g3d-storm, every frame carried onto the camera of 4980): M has no eye, no plain and no ridge at the place; its structure stands still through the 16 frames. S is weighed in over M three ways: by the eye's height (globe.height 0.9 to 0.15 radii, far.height), by the distance from the eye inside the scene (far.distance, 3 to 8 camera heights), and by a border 16 to 26 degrees from the place. On main the height law gives S 0.85 at 4984, 0.40 at 4990, 0.03 at 4996 (my sums): nearly half of the exchange in your six frames. The second and third laws are the decal's edge and they move with the camera: hence the patch that shrinks in open view, the cut ends of the ridge and the dark navy border. My rounds 41 and 42 moved these laws; moving them cannot remove them.
Review tier: 4987 is attached (70 samples, 416 s at preview). All 16 frames cost about 1 h 50 min here (64 to 74 samples each); I stopped that render to make the proofs above. Plain every-frame sheets of 4980 to 4995 at draft are attached (ev-767). Say if you still want the 16 at review; I would rather spend the time on the cure.

C. THE PLAN: HOW (1), (2), (3) GO AT THE CAUSE

(1) Sky. Cause (read from my recipe and the engine's code and from the critics' frames; my own control comes with the commit): `sky.json` lays two painted pictures into the sky, each at a fixed aim, and the engine weighs them against its own sky across the dive and the rise: `orbit` (the hero's sky) and `terrain` (the approved close image's sky, margin 12.5 percent). (2) and (3) One field, by place only.

If the hero's field alone rules, 4860 loses its picture.
So:
(i) The planet's field is M everywhere, at every height and distance, read by the globe's own lines.
(ii) The eye, the plain and the ridge become permanent small objects of the planet, each a function of the ground point with a natural end of its own (the ridge tapers out, the plain's tone falls to M's deck). The globe and the scene draw them with the same functions at full weight always.

(iv) Deleted: globe.height, far.height, far.distance, globe.border, and with them every law that weighs one picture against another by height or by distance from the eye. Nothing is left to dissolve and nothing is finite.

Cause read in `deep.ts` (not yet shown by a frame): the cast of the cirrus on the deck reads the cirrus with a foot of twice the pixel's (`cirrusInside(gs, max(2.0 * fp, castWave))`); with a foot larger than a streamer's fibres the noise is cut to its mean and the threshold of the mean fills the whole lee fringe (3 units) as one sheet, where the fine field is sparse fibres. A threshold of a mean is not the mean of the thresholds, so from afar the shadow is a full sheet with a hard border, and the body over it is missed by the march (a step is 0.002 of the distance). 3 (b) of MAIL 806 is not met there.

The cut of the octaves, the foot of the cirrus and the steps of the march follow it, so a capture at 3840 carries one octave more than a render at 1920 and the thresholded shapes (fibres, their shadows) can differ. With 1 - T = 0.25 over a dark deck the air comes through as 0.25^2.6 = 0.027 of S in red, 0.25^3.1 = 0.014 in green, 0.25^3.7 = 0.006 in blue: thin air lifted the plain by almost nothing and four and a half times more in red than in blue. At the ground the grade is none and the law is L = L0 * T + S * (1 - T) to the letter. The veil keeps `underAir` (not touched, said as open).

## Way C (MAIL 1011 point 2): how I read it, written before the first render of it (09:48 UTC)

What the code does today: the scene works in the colours of the ground (the full grade), and its end raises every channel to
`uFallPower` = (1 + fall (P - 1)) / P about the pivot; the globe is graded by `fallGrade` with the power 1 + fall (P - 1). fall is a
law of the eye's height alone (1.9 to 0.25 radii). That is the curve that changes with the eye's height.

Term (a): fall is 0 at every height. Then the end's power is 1 / P everywhere, which is what the hold has, so 4605 and every frame of
4530 to 4679 keep their bits by construction (the uniforms there are the same numbers as today). Control B0 (deep.json, fall.height
[0.002, 0.001]) is running to show what that picture is at 4860 and what the two pairs read.

Term (b): the air between the eye and each thing. A thing whose colour the hold shows as H is seen from above through the whole air
over it: H = X Tf + A (1 - Tf), X the thing as the dimmed Sun lights it, A the lit air's colour, Tf what the whole path through the
air lets through. An eye inside the air has a shorter path, Tp: L = X Tp + A (1 - Tp) = H + (X - A) (Tp - Tf). With X - A =
(H - A) exp(tau), tau the air straight over the thing by colour (red most): L = H + (H - A) exp(tau) (Tp - Tf). Above the air
Tp = Tf and the picture is H to the bit. Near ground under an eye in the air: darker than H where H is under A (navy), far ground:
Tp falls to Tf and the picture is H (pale). It reads the thing's height, the eye's place and the ray, never the clock.

  thing, H, is two lights: the thing's own (the Sun's light dimmed by the air above the lit point, a gain g by colour, then let
  through by the air of the whole ray) and the light of the lit air in front of it (the rest). An eye inside the air has a part
  of that air in front: L = H ((1 - g exp(-all)) share + g exp(-between)), share = (1 - exp(-between)) / (1 - exp(-all)). At the
  top all = between and L = H to the bit. Every term is a share of H: nothing goes under nothing, no tint. The air is thin at the
  deck and thickest some way up (exp(-h / scale) - exp(-h / foot)), so the eye of the terrain stands under most of it.
  deep.json air: top, scale, foot, depth (the whole air straight up, by colour), sun (the dimming of the Sun at the deck, by
  colour), cirrus (the share of its own light in what the hold shows of a cirrus: it is white up there, so nearly all).
- C6p (scale 8, foot 1.5, depth 1.4 1.1 1.0, sun 3.2 2.7 2.5, the cirrus as the deck): a smooth navy, darker near, paler far, NO
  hard specks; but the streamer is dimmed too and goes brown, and the far ground stays dark. G17 proxy 0.297, p25 0.089.
  Shares of H (linear): low left 0.18, mid 0.24, far plain 0.35, right plain 0.31, far right 0.44, near limb 0.5. Wanted by the
  approved: low left 0.18 0.12 0.09 (red green blue), mid 1.0 0.48 0.35, far plain 0.88 0.69 0.56, right plain 1.8 1.1 0.88.
- C7p (cirrus 0.85, foot 3, depth 2.6 1.8 1.5, sun 2.6 2.4 2.4): white streamer on navy ground, paler to the limb, pale haze at
  the limb, no specks. G17 proxy 0.433, p25 0.089 (c2edd61ba 0.508, 0.128). Tones: low left (3, 18, 45) against the approved
  (3, 12, 26); far plain (30, 70, 121) against (54, 107, 158); right plain (32, 67, 113) against (106, 149, 189); mid (18, 49, 88)
  against (59, 87, 122). The far ground is still too dark.
- A limit I see by arithmetic, to be said in the mail: air in layers gives a path to the ground of 1 / sin of the angle down, so
  between the near box (42 degrees down) and the far plain (16 degrees) the path grows 3 times and no more. The approved's shares
  grow 5 to 6 times from near to far. So layered air can make near dark and far paler, but not as much paler as the painting.
